Projects.question: Tell me about your Superstore ETL Pipeline project.
Projects.answer: An Azure Data Factory pipeline that ingests, transforms, and loads Superstore retail sales data from CSV into Azure SQL, feeding a downstream Power BI analytics dashboard. It uses a Copy Data activity to move data from Azure Blob Storage into Azure SQL, and was validated end-to-end through ADF's debug and output logs.

Projects.question: Tell me about your final year project.
Projects.answer: A sensor-based smart park-and-ride reservation system for integrated transport hubs in Sri Lanka, designed to motivate commuters to use park-and-ride facilities and reduce congestion. When a user makes a reservation, they receive a QR code; when an attendant scans that QR code, the gate opens automatically via a servo motor. Parking slots use IR sensors to detect real-time occupancy. It's currently semi-automated, with a roadmap to become a fully automated, sensor-driven system.

Projects.question: What technologies does your final year project use?
Projects.answer: Spring Boot for the backend, Next.js and Tailwind CSS for the frontend, and IoT hardware — servo motors for automated gate control and IR sensors on each slot for real-time occupancy detection — for the physical, sensor-based side of the system.

Projects.question: Do you have IoT or hardware/sensor experience?
Projects.answer: Yes — my final year project is a hardware-integrated IoT system. It uses IR sensors on parking slots for real-time occupancy detection and a servo motor to automatically open the gate once an attendant scans a user's reservation QR code.

Projects.question: Do you have experience with automation or cloud-native systems?
Projects.answer: Yes, in two ways: my final year project automates physical access control (QR-code-triggered servo gates and IR sensor-based slot detection), and I've also built cloud data automation with an Azure Data Factory ETL pipeline that automates ingesting and loading retail data into Azure SQL.

Projects.question: How does the QR code and gate system work in your final year project?
Projects.answer: When a commuter makes a reservation, the system generates a QR code for them. On arrival, an attendant scans the QR code, which verifies the reservation and automatically triggers a servo motor to open the gate — no manual gate control needed.

Projects.question: How does slot detection work in your final year project?
Projects.answer: Each parking slot has an IR sensor that detects in real time whether the slot is occupied or free, so the reservation system always reflects live slot availability.

Projects.question: Is your final year project fully automated?
Projects.answer: It's semi-automated right now — QR verification and gate opening are automated, and slots are monitored live via IR sensors. The plan is to expand this into a fully automated, end-to-end sensor-driven system.

Projects.question: Can I see a live version of your final year project?
Projects.answer: Yes, it's deployed at https://smartpark-reservation-frontend.vercel.app/
